_doc: Street furniture and crosswalks: the one owner of where every lamp, signal post, hydrant, bin, bench and street tree stands and where the crosswalk and stop line lie (native/src/sim/roads/street_furniture.cpp). The walkers keep off each piece's footprint; the render draws, lights and wires them from these places (how they look is data/render/streets.json). Every distance below cites its primary source; arcs are metres from the arm's mouth (its setback, which lies past the crossing street's kerb line), offsets metres from the kerb's face.

sidewalk._doc: ABNT NBR 9050:2020 and Sao Paulo Decree 52.903/12 art. 14 par. 1: a free width of at least 1.20 m kept for walking; Decree 45.904/05 art. 7: furniture, poles and trees only in the service strip next to the kerb. Calcadas Cariocas (Rio de Janeiro, 2026), Faixa Utilitaria: the face of every pole and urban element at least 0.50 m from the kerb. A piece other than a lamp or signal post stands only where its far edge leaves the free width. height_m: the footway's top over the carriageway, where the walkers stand (sim/traffic/lane_geometry.cpp) and the render lays the footway, its furniture and a tram's flush track (render/roads, render/props, render/transit).

lamps._doc: The street's lamps hang on the utility poles that carry its wires, one row on one face; no lighting column stands on the other face, so the poles of the power line are the street's only poles (a pole carries lamp and wires: Enel SP PD-4.003, urban overhead distribution networks; Rioluz NPIP-1 5.2, the line on one face). Basic span span_m 35 m (PD-4.003); the poles spread evenly from one end of the block to the other, one past each crosswalk (Rioluz NPIP-1 item 4: a crossing is lit by the sum of both streets). The line stands on the east or south face (NPIP-1 5.2). pool_*: the night pool of a lamp, across: pool_share of the carriageway plus pool_margin_m, at least pool_least_m, its middle pool_back_m short of that from the pole (modelling choices, no norm found). reach_m is measured on props.pole in data/render/streets.json: the lens 1.6 m out along its bracket.

furniture._doc: Bins and benches. Prefeitura de São Paulo, Programa Passeio Livre: small and medium furniture 5 m from the corner's axis. Anchieta (ES) Lei 1.215/2017 on litter bins: at least 50 m apart, preferably at the corners, so one bin at each corner of a full-furniture street outside industrial zones whose block is at least bin_spacing_m long. A bench stands in the middle of residential blocks.

trees._doc: Prefeitura de São Paulo, Manual Técnico de Arborização Urbana (SVMA, 2015), for the medium trees the town plants (6 to 9 m tall): table 01, a sidewalk of at least 1.90 m (1.20 m free + 0.70 m service strip) and a pit of at least 0.60 m; item 4.1, the pit at least 0.10 m from the kerb; table 03, 5 m from the corner, 1 m from a crosswalk's edge, 2 m from hydrants and urban furniture, 8 m from the next tree. Rioluz NPIP-1 5.2: poles at least 5 m from a tree pit (stricter than the manual's 3 m).

poles._doc: The utility poles the player strings (Street tab) and the planner of a run. height_m: the pole clear of the ground, 12.0 m: a 14 m distribution pole (a nominal length of ABNT NBR 8451-1, concrete poles for distribution networks) set L/10 + 0.60 m = 2.0 m deep, the embedding of Neoenergia DIS-NOR-012 rev. 08 table 30, which sets a 12 m pole 1.8 m deep; its mesh is props.pole of data/render/streets.json. max_spacing_m: DIS-NOR-012 6.6.31.9: spans of 30 to 40 m. kerb_inset_m: sidewalk.kerb_clear_m plus the radius of the mast. The rest are behaviour of the tool, with no norm: how near a pointer catches the line, how close two poles may stand, how far a run looks for its way (route_margin), the step of the guide lines along the footways it is planned on (guide_step_m), what crossing a street costs over its width, and which bend counts as a corner (a pole with its own arm per line).

barriers._doc: Walls, fences and hedges traced by the player, and the guardrail and railing at the kerb. guardrail: a W-beam on posts every 2.00 m (NBR 6971 through DER-PR ES-OC 07/18). The other heights and thicknesses carry no norm and follow the Roadcraft 4.0 look. footway_reach_m: how far from the back of a footway a point is still put on it; kerb_gap_m and back_gap_m: the clearance behind the kerb stone and past the back of the footway.

signs._doc: The signs the rules put up and how far a placed plate governs an approach, as the Roadcraft 4.0 places them (no norm): the rule's plate a metre past the stop line, the speed plate 14 m past the mouth of a stretch of at least 60 m, a name plate 1.5 m past the mouth. approach_reach_m: how far back from a mouth a placed Stop or Give Way is still the rule of that approach. plate_kerb_m: the post from the kerb, by style. far_share: no plate past this share of a short segment. The drawings and sizes of the plates are data/render/streets.json signs.

items._doc: What the player places on the footway, as the Roadcraft 4.0 tool does (no norm). gap_m: the room kept between two items. stand_reach_m: how far off its band an item still stands on a footway. meadow_apart_m: clumps of long grass keep apart. cut_reach_m: a piece of the street kit taken away by the player is matched by its place within this. median_reach_m: how far from the centre line of a planted median a plant is still put on it. demolish_reach_m: how near a click takes a street piece before it takes the road under it.

street_names._doc: The name a street without one is given (sim/street/street_names.cpp), as Roadcraft 4.0 world/roads/streetNames.ts names them. names: the list, by style; empty, the streets go unnamed (styles.eua and styles.europa until they have their own). prefix: the word before it; prefixes: for a road category or a profile id, the word that takes its place. reach_m: how far from a street its name may stand and still name it.

footprints._doc: Ground each kind covers at walking height, [x_m, z_m] in its own frame (x along the sidewalk and z toward the road for the kerbside pieces; a signal post's z faces the arriving traffic), measured on its mesh in data/render/streets.json props: the pole, trunk (at the largest street tree) or body; arms, heads and crowns are overhead. lamp_column, post_box, phone and kerb_drain are their bodies in streets.json; shrub its planted width; utility_pole the foot of the mast (poles.height_m); sign_post the room a walker keeps from the plate.

styles._doc: What changes with a city's regional style (session-rules.md, section 10), laid over this table by DataTables: a block here replaces the same keys above, a list replaces the list. signals: the same in both for now, nothing of the Roadcraft 4.0 was measured to tell them apart.

roadcraft._doc: What the Roadcraft 4.0 draws. plate_kerb_m: carried from brasil, the 4.0's was not measured. hydrants.reach_m: 100, the 4.0's hydrant every 100 m on one side, which this rule's squares of coverage reach at about 10 a km, as it counts. furniture: bins and benches in rows, every 60 m from 9 and 24 m past the mouth, up to 4 m from the end (world/roads/furnitureCatalog.ts); trees: its generated city has none on the footway (editor/cityGenerator.ts), a street the player draws does.

signals._doc: CONTRAN MBST vol. V (Res. 483/2014), 9.1.1: one pattern, here 'after the crossing street'; table 10.4: a head on an arm over the road at 5.50 m stands at least 13 m past the stop line, which the far side of the junction gives. The post stands on the far arm, at the right of the traffic going straight on, just clear of that arm's crosswalk (9.2.3 c: never in front of the dropped kerb); 9.1.5: columns usually 0.80 m from the kerb (never under 0.30 m). An approach with no straight continuation (the stem of a T) keeps its post on its own corner, the exception 9.1.1 allows.

hydrants._doc: Corpo de Bombeiros do Paraná NPT 034 (urban hydrants), 5.1.2.2 a) and 5.2.4: each covers a radius of at most reach_m, preferably at street corners. The town is cut into squares reach_m / √2 wide (any point of one is within reach_m of any other), each holding one hydrant at the corner of its node nearest the square's centre.

crossing._doc: As the Roadcraft 4.0 draws it (src/world/approach.ts): the zebra 1.2 m past the mouth and 3 m deep, the stop line 0.64 m behind it and 0.4 m wide. Not a norm: the look of this style.

brasil._doc: plate_kerb_curve_m: a plate clears the road by 0.40 m in a curve where it clears it by 0.30 m on the straight (MBST vol. I 3.7), so its post stands 0.10 m further in. plate_kerb_m: CONTRAN MBST vol. I (2022) 3.11: a plate edge at least 0.30 m off the carriageway on a straight, with the 0.45 m half of the widest plate, R-2.

signals._doc: CONTRAN MBST vol. V (Res. 483/2014), 9.1.1: one pattern, here 'after the crossing street'; table 10.4: a head on an arm over the road at 5.50 m stands at least 13 m past the stop line, which the far side of the junction gives. The post stands on the far arm, at the right of the traffic going straight on, just clear of that arm's crosswalk (9.2.3 c: never in front of the dropped kerb); 9.1.5: columns usually 0.80 m from the kerb (never under 0.30 m). An approach with no straight continuation (the stem of a T) keeps its post on its own corner, the exception 9.1.1 allows.

hydrants._doc: Corpo de Bombeiros do Paraná NPT 034 (urban hydrants), 5.1.2.2 a) and 5.2.4: each covers a radius of at most reach_m, preferably at street corners. The town is cut into squares reach_m / √2 wide (any point of one is within reach_m of any other), each holding one hydrant at the corner of its node nearest the square's centre.

crossing._doc: CONTRAN MBST vol. IV (Res. 973/2022): 5.4, a zebra crossing (FTP-1) at least 1.00 m from the crossing street's kerb line and 3.00 m wide, 4.00 m recommended; 5.1, the stop line (LRE) 0.30 to 0.60 m wide, at least 1.60 m before the crosswalk. Vehicles stop with their front at the line; walkers cross along the zebra's middle and keep to its right half.

eua._doc: To fill from the MUTCD (FHWA) and the AASHTO Green Book.

europa._doc: To fill from the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals (1968) and the European norms.
